chapter_title: Designing an A/B Test with Students
learning_objective: The learner will apply the data-minimization practices to ten possible data items by sorting each into Collect, Replace with a code, or Do not collect, with at least 9 of 10 correct on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** privacy-data-sorter
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Apply
**Bloom Verb:** apply
**Learning Objective:** The learner will apply the data-minimization practices to ten possible data items by sorting each into Collect, Replace with a code, or Do not collect, with at least 9 of 10 correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** Student Privacy in Testing, Informed Consent, Pre-Test, Post-Test (all defined in this chapter above this block). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each item the learner commits one of three bins. A placement is correct when it matches the Correct bin column in Content. Mastery is at least 9 of 10 correct on the first attempt. Reading the six practices is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) More data makes a better test. (2) Replacing a name with a code makes the key unnecessary to protect. (3) A birthdate is needed to know a student's grade level. **Instructional Rationale:** Sorting data items by what the question needs is an Apply-level use of data minimization. Ten items that cover the scores, the identifiers, and the contact details teach the learner to ask whether each item answers the research question. **Content:** The three bins: Collect (keep it in the data file), Replace with a code (keep it only in the separate key file), Do not collect. The ten items (all for the Watershed Basics pilot): | # | Data item | Correct bin | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | Pre-test score | Collect | The gain cannot be computed without it. | | 2 | Post-test score | Collect | The gain cannot be computed without it. | | 3 | Which version the student used | Collect | The comparison depends on it. | | 4 | Grade level | Collect | It describes the sample without identifying a student. | | 5 | Student name | Replace with a code | The name belongs only in the separate key file. | | 6 | School student ID number | Replace with a code | The ID identifies the student, so only a code goes in the data. | | 7 | Email address | Do not collect | The test does not need it. | | 8 | Home address | Do not collect | The test does not need it. | | 9 | Birthdate | Do not collect | Grade level answers the question without it. | | 10 | Photograph of the student working | Do not collect | It identifies the student and the test does not need it. | **Provenance:** The items are illustrative examples written for this chapter, and the sim labels them "illustrative examples". The practices follow the chapter section "Student Privacy in Testing". The sim adds the note "your school's rules decide". **Rules:** Each item has exactly one correct bin. Four items are Collect, two are Replace with a code, and four are Do not collect. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees one item and the three bins, and may open the six practices. Opening them does not change the score. 2. The learner places the item in a bin, and the placement is committed. 3. The sim shows whether it was correct and the Why text. 4. After item 10 the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 10 items in a shuffled order, one attempt each. Correct: "Correct: [bin]. [Why]". Incorrect: "Not quite. This item belongs in [bin]. [Why]". The summary shows "[n] of 10 correct on the first attempt". At 9 or more it adds "You can collect only what the test needs." Below 9 it lists the Why text of each missed item. **Starting State:** The first item in the shuffled order and the three bins. The question shown is "Does the test need this item, and in what form?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter's first two practices are to collect only what the question needs and to use a code in place of a name. The sim applies both.
